goal: Evaluate whether the target model answers questions grounded in a short provided document packet, citing supporting evidence and avoiding unsupported claims.

spec.objective: Evaluate whether the target model answers questions grounded in a short provided document packet, citing supporting evidence and avoiding unsupported claims.

dimensions.name: Direct Fact Extraction and Citation
dimensions.description: Test whether the model correctly extracts a single factual statement from the document and cites the exact supporting sentence.
dimensions.approach: Provide a short document (2–3 sentences) with a clear fact. Ask a question whose answer is directly present in the document. Score based on correctness and citation accuracy.
item_requirements: Generate a short document (3–5 sentences) and a question that has a clear answer present in the document. The answer should be a single fact. Ensure the document contains a sentence that directly answers the question. The model must output an answer with a citation to the exact sentence. Avoid ambiguous or multi-fact questions. The scoring judge will check: 1) factual correctness, 2) correct sentence cited, 3) no extra unsupported claims.

dimensions.name: Multi-fact Answer with Multiple Citations
dimensions.description: Test whether the model can aggregate multiple facts from the document, citing each fact appropriately.
dimensions.approach: Provide a document with several related facts. Ask a question that requires combining multiple pieces of information. Score based on completeness and citation for each fact.

dimensions.name: Refusal to Answer Unsupported Queries
dimensions.description: Test whether the model declines to answer or states 'not supported' when the question cannot be answered from the given document.
dimensions.approach: Provide a document that does not contain the answer to the question. The model should not fabricate an answer.

dimensions.name: Ambiguity and Contradiction Handling
dimensions.description: Test how the model handles documents with ambiguous or contradictory statements, requiring careful citation or qualification.
dimensions.approach: Provide a document that contains statements that could be interpreted in multiple ways or are contradictory. Ask a question that requires the model to note the ambiguity or contradiction.

dimensions.name: Citation Format and Precision
dimensions.description: Test whether the model adheres to a specified citation format and cites precise spans (e.g., sentence number or exact quote) rather than vague references.
dimensions.approach: Provide a document and ask the model to answer with citations in a specific format, e.g., [sentence 2] or quote. Evaluate format compliance and precision.

dimensions.name: Groundedness Amidst Irrelevant Information
dimensions.description: Test whether the model ignores irrelevant or distractor information in the document and only uses relevant facts to answer.
dimensions.approach: Provide a document that contains both relevant and irrelevant information. Ask a question that only requires a subset. The model should not include irrelevant details.

constraints: All items must include a short document packet (100–500 words).
The model must base its answer solely on the provided document.
Each answer must include explicit citations (e.g., sentence numbers, quotes).
No external knowledge or pretraining memory should be used.
spec.planner_notes: Six dimensions, each with three items (total 18 items) to cover core groundedness and citation skills at L4 difficulty. All items are self-generated (no external sources needed) because synthetic short documents are sufficient and controllable. The primary task type is open_generation with a judge scoring both factual accuracy and citation quality. Dimensions test: direct extraction, multi-fact aggregation, appropriate refusal, ambiguity handling, citation format compliance, and ignoring irrelevant content.

critique.notes: All six checklist items are fully covered. The spec defines a clear objective (grounded QA with citation), targets deepseek-chat, uses open_generation task type across six dimensions, covers content including extraction, multi-fact, refusal, ambiguity, format, and distractor handling, sets a mid scale of 18 items, and specifies accuracy and judge_score as metrics. Each dimension has concrete item_requirements for generation and scoring.

items.rubric:
Score 1–5:

3: Answer is correct but citation is missing or wrong sentence number.
2: Answer is partially correct but cites wrong sentence or includes unsupported claim.
1: Answer is incorrect, or fabricates information.
0: No answer provided.

dataset.generation_notes:
direct_fact_extraction: Generated 3 open_generation items for the Direct Fact Extraction and Citation dimension. Each item includes a short document (3–5 sentences) with a single clear fact, a question directly answerable from one sentence, and instructions to answer with citation by sentence number. The rubric defines five score levels with 1 point each for factual correctness, correct citation, proper format, and absence of extra claims. All content is self-generated (no external sources).
multi_fact_with_multiple_citations: Three open_generation items for the multi_fact_with_multiple_citations dimension. Each item provides a synthetic document (5–7 sentences, at least 3 distinct facts) and a question requiring at least 2 facts. The model must cite supporting sentences by number in brackets (e.g., [Sentence 3]). Topics: renewable energy project, company history, library design – chosen to avoid overlap. Rubrics check factual correctness, correct citations per fact, and no hallucination.
refusal_unsupported_queries: Three open_generation items for the 'refusal_unsupported_queries' dimension. Each provides a short synthetic document (3-5 sentences) on a distinct topic (product features, health study, university policy) and asks about a feature or detail not mentioned in the document. The model must appropriately state that the document lacks the information rather than fabricating an answer. Rubrics are provided for judge scoring on three criteria: no fabrication, appropriate refusal, and no hallucinated citations.
ambiguity_contradiction_handling: Three open_generation items for the Ambiguity and Contradiction Handling dimension. Each item provides a short document (4–6 sentences) containing either ambiguous phrasing or two sentences that appear contradictory but are reconciled by different contexts. The questions require the model to identify the nuance, cite both relevant sentences by number in brackets, and avoid oversimplification. Rubrics check: (1) correct identification of ambiguity/contradiction, (2) citations point to the correct sentences, (3) answer does not oversimplify. Topics are diverse: financial reporting, workplace policy, and medical research.
citation_format_precision: Generated 3 open_generation items for the 'Citation Format and Precision' dimension. Each item includes a short document (3-4 sentences), a single-fact question, and an explicit instruction to cite by sentence number in brackets. Items cover: direct extraction with one citation, selective extraction from a multi-sentence document, and multi-sentence citation. Edge cases tested: ignoring irrelevant information and citing multiple sentences. All sources are self-generated. Scoring rubric focuses on factual correctness, citation format compliance, and correct sentence attribution.
grounded_irrelevant_information: Three items for Groundedness Amidst Irrelevant Information dimension. Each includes a 7-sentence document with 1-2 relevant sentences and 5-6 irrelevant sentences. The model must answer a factual question by citing the relevant sentence(s) in brackets and ignoring irrelevant information. Diversified across biography, product launch, and scientific study domains.
